newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON SAYS HE HAS FIGHT ON HAND TO DEFEND TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON SAYS HE HAS FIGHT ON HAND TO DEFEND TITLE.

text.p: Allen Johnson cruised into the semifinals of the men's high hurdles at the world championships on Tuesday but conceded he faced a fierce battle to retain his title.

The Olympic champion hardly brushed a hurdle on his way to a comfortable second-round victory in 13.22 seconds which took him into Wednesday's semifinals. The American Olympic champion then said the final on Thursday was likely to be a tight affair because the Athens track was so fast.

"It was decent. I got off balance in the middle but I managed to work it out," he said. "I was chopping my step because the track is so fast. It is going to be really good (in the final). Very competitive. Like four or five guys leaning for the tape. Of course I think I can come out first."
American Mark Crear, who won the silver medal at the Atlanta Games, sent a warning to Johnson of his fine form when he beat Britain's world record holder Colin Jackson in his heat.

Crear pipped Jackson on the line to win in 13.15 seconds. Jackson, whose 13.19 was the fastest time of the first round earlier in the day, finished second in the same time to go through to the semifinals.
Jackson has a lot to prove after injury forced him to concede his world title to Johnson in 1995 and lack of form deprived him of an Olympic medal in Atlanta when he finished fourth.
"It was nice, neat and compact," he said of his race. "I am satisfied. Until you get the pressure it doesn't get urgent. It was nice and relaxed."
His compatriot Tony Jarrett, the silver medallist in the 1995 world championships in Gothenburg, also had few problems, winning his heat in 13.27 seconds.
Germany's Florian Schwarthoff, the bronze medallist in Atlanta, also looked smooth, taking third in the last heat in 13.30 to reach the semifinals.
